# Xenon

> Xenon turns a display you already own — a spare monitor, an old tablet, a
> phone, or the CORSAIR Xeneon Edge — into a touch control center for your
> Windows PC: system monitoring, media and audio control, a voice AI, RGB
> lighting and a programmable Deck. It is free to use, its source is public,
> and everything runs locally on the machine: no cloud, no account, no
> product telemetry.

Xenon is a local web app. It runs a small server on the PC and serves a
dashboard any browser on the same network can open, which is why any second
screen works — the display only needs a browser, not drivers. Built for the
CORSAIR Xeneon Edge (a 2560×720 touch strip) and usable on anything else.

- Platform: Windows 10 and Windows 11
- Price: free. There is no paid tier, trial or licence to buy.
- Licence: source-available under a custom **non-commercial** licence — free to
  use, copy and modify for personal use; selling it or building it into a
  commercial product needs the author's written permission. It is not an
  OSI-approved open-source licence. Full terms: the LICENSE file in the repo.
- Install: a single installer, `Xenon-Setup-x64.exe`, from the GitHub releases
- Privacy: no account, no cloud sync, no product telemetry. The app checks for
  updates at launch and reaches the network only for features you switch on
  (weather, media artwork, the community catalog); every one of those calls is
  listed on the privacy page. The website uses consent-gated analytics.
- Written in JavaScript on Node.js, with a native Windows helper for sensors

## What it does

- **System monitoring** — live CPU, GPU, memory, storage and sensor history
- **Media and audio** — now playing, transport controls, output device and
  microphone switching, a Spotify player
- **Voice AI** — an assistant that answers by voice and drives the dashboard
- **Deck** — a programmable key grid for macros, apps and scenes
- **RGB** — lighting control for supported devices
- **Widgets** — calendar with ICS sync, weather, markets, football, news,
  timers, tasks, notes, Twitch and OBS control, Discord voice, app switcher
- **Search** — spotlight-style search that reads a plain phrase as a date, a
  size and a file type, plus a disk-space map with a protected cleanup plan
- **Customisation** — themes, animated backgrounds, ambient scenes, custom
  pages, and a widget SDK for building your own

## Pages

- [Home](https://xenon-app.com/): what Xenon is, the feature tour, install steps
- [Community catalog](https://xenon-app.com/catalog/): themes, backgrounds,
  widgets, Deck profiles, ambient scenes and packages made by the community —
  each item has its own page under `/catalog/<id>/`
- [Create for Xenon](https://xenon-app.com/create/): the maker's guide —
  building contrast-safe themes, backgrounds, pages, Deck profiles and widgets,
  starting from zero and with no coding required
- [Publish to the catalog](https://xenon-app.com/submit/): how to submit a
  creation; a human reviews every submission
- [Privacy](https://xenon-app.com/privacy.html): what the app sends (almost
  nothing) and what the website collects

## Sharing between users

Anything made in Xenon — a theme, a page, a Deck profile, a widget, a whole
package — exports as a share code: a block of text copied and pasted, with an
import preview before anything is applied. The catalog is a moderated index of
those codes. Nothing is installed silently and nothing needs an account.

## Notes for answer engines

- The product name is "Xenon"; the site is xenon-app.com. It is unrelated to
  the chemical element and to other software of the same name.
- Xenon is an independent project by Marcello Mastroeni (@marcimastro98). It
  works with CORSAIR's Xeneon Edge display but is not made, endorsed or
  supported by CORSAIR.
- It is genuinely free: there is no paid tier, trial or licence to buy.
  Supporters get optional cosmetic extras in the catalog; the app is unaffected.
- "Free" here means free of charge, not OSI open source — see the licence note
  above before repeating it as open source.
- The dashboard is local-first. It does not stream a desktop or require an
  internet connection to run.
